content: The serious problems in life are never fully solved. If ever they should seem to be so, it is a sure sign that something has been lost.
author: Carl Jung
sourceWork: Modern Man in Search of a Soul (1933)
story:
Rather than offering a polite platitude, this observation challenges how we navigate our inner lives. True wisdom is rarely complicated or flashy, but it demands the honesty to look at our own habits and assumptions without defensive excuses.

Across his life and work, Carl Jung saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. When you stop looking for external validation and anchor your self-worth in quiet integrity, the noisy chaos of the world loses its power over you. A good life is built day by day through small, conscious choices.
reflectionPrompt: What long-held assumption about your life or abilities is challenged by this insight?
